title: Module 7 · Adult Critical Care
intro: Pressors and steroids, extravasation, analgesia first sedation and PRIS, hyperkalemia, hyponatremia correction, ICU glucose, DKA with the 2024 consensus, IV potassium, stress ulcer prophylaxis and an ICU night.

cases.title: Which pressor and in what order?
cases.stem: After 30 mL/kg of fluid, MAP is 58. Norepinephrine is started and is now at 0.3 mcg/kg/min, MAP 62.

steps.q: What is the MAP goal?

options.why: Higher targets add pressor harm without benefit for most patients.

steps.q: What does SSC 2021 suggest next?

options.t: Add vasopressin rather than raising norepinephrine further
options.why: Vasopressin works on a different receptor (V1).

steps.q: Norepinephrine has been at or above 0.25 mcg/kg/min for 4 hours. What else is suggested?

options.t: Hydrocortisone 200 mg/day IV (50 mg every 6 hours or an infusion)

steps.q: If heart function is poor with low output despite MAP 65, what may be added?

options.why: Squeezing more does not fix a weak pump.

cases.pearl: **Norepi to MAP 65, add vasopressin, hydrocortisone if 0.25 or more for 4 h, dobutamine for a weak heart.**

sources.t: Evans L, et al. Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021. Crit Care Med 2021;49:e1063-e1143

cases.title: Peripheral norepinephrine and extravasation
cases.stem: Norepinephrine was started through a forearm IV while the central line is placed. The site is now pale and cold.

steps.q: What is the antidote and dose?

options.t: Phentolamine 5 to 10 mg diluted in 10 to 15 mL normal saline, infiltrated into the area as soon as possible

options.why: Used for some other extravasations, not vasopressors.

steps.q: What else do you tell the nurse?

options.t: Stop the infusion at that site, aspirate what you can, remove the catheter, restart the pressor at another site, elevate the limb
options.why: Never let the pressor stop: its effect ends in minutes.

cases.pearl: **Pressor leak: phentolamine 5 to 10 mg in 10 to 15 mL NS, restart pressor elsewhere.**

sources.t: FDA label, Norepinephrine Bitartrate in Sodium Chloride (2022)

cases.title: Analgesia first
cases.stem: A ventilated patient is agitated. The resident wants to start midazolam.

steps.q: What does PADIS 2018 recommend first?

options.t: Treat pain first (analgesia first), using CPOT or BPS if the patient cannot report pain

options.why: Benzodiazepines prolong ventilation and raise delirium.

steps.q: If sedation is still needed, which agents are preferred?

options.t: Propofol or dexmedetomidine over benzodiazepines, targeting light sedation

steps.q: Should haloperidol be given routinely to prevent delirium?

options.t: No: PADIS recommends against routine antipsychotics to prevent or treat delirium
options.why: Screen with CAM-ICU or ICDSC and fix causes.

cases.pearl: **Analgesia first, light sedation, propofol or dex over benzos, no routine antipsychotics.**

sources.t: Devlin JW, et al. PADIS guideline. Crit Care Med 2018;46:e825-e873

cases.title: Propofol infusion syndrome
cases.stem: Propofol at 80 mcg/kg/min for 4 days with norepinephrine. New metabolic acidosis, rising CK and triglycerides 620 mg/dL.

steps.q: What do you suspect?

options.why: Risk rises above about 4 mg/kg/h (about 67 mcg/kg/min) and after 48 hours, especially with catecholamines or steroids.
The pattern points to the drug.

steps.q: What do you recommend?

options.t: Stop propofol and switch to another sedative

options.why: Not enough when PRIS is suspected.

steps.q: What do you monitor on long propofol infusions?

options.t: Triglycerides and CK, plus pancreatitis signs; count propofol lipid calories in nutrition

cases.pearl: **Propofol above 67 mcg/kg/min, over 48 h, acidosis + CK + TG = PRIS. Stop it.**

sources.t: Kam PCA, Cardone D. Propofol infusion syndrome. Anaesthesia 2007;62:690-701
Devlin JW, et al. PADIS guideline. Crit Care Med 2018;46:e825-e873

cases.title: Hyperkalemia with ECG changes
cases.stem: K 7.1 mmol/L, peaked T waves, CrCl 15 mL/min, glucose 110.

steps.q: What goes first?

options.t: Calcium gluconate 1 g (10 mL of 10%) IV over 2 to 5 minutes, repeat if ECG changes persist
options.why: Protects the heart; does not lower potassium. Some protocols use 3 g.

steps.q: Then shift potassium. With her kidney failure, which insulin dose?

options.t: Regular insulin 5 units IV with dextrose 25 g, glucose checks hourly for 4 to 6 hours
options.why: Kidney failure slows insulin clearance, so late hypoglycemia is common.

steps.q: How will the potassium actually leave the body?

options.t: A binder (sodium zirconium cyclosilicate 10 g or patiromer 8.4 g), and dialysis with her kidney failure
options.why: Insulin only hides potassium in cells for a few hours.

cases.pearl: **Protect (calcium), shift (insulin + dextrose, 5 units in kidney failure), remove (binder, diuretic, dialysis).**

sources.t: Clase CM, et al. Potassium homeostasis and management of dyskalemia (KDIGO). Kidney Int 2020;97:42-61
St. Mary's ICU drip concentrations, electrolyte and insulin protocols (verify locally)

workup.calc: K 7.1 with peaked T waves = severe. Calcium gluconate 1 g now; regular insulin **5 units** (CrCl 15) + dextrose 25 g; glucose hourly x 4 to 6 h; binder and dialysis.

cases.title: Severe hyponatremia with a seizure

steps.q: What is the emergency treatment?

options.t: 3% saline bolus (100 to 150 mL over 10 to 20 minutes), repeat up to about 3 times, aiming for a 4 to 6 mmol/L rise

steps.q: What is the limit on correction?

options.t: About 10 mmol/L in the first 24 hours and 8 per 24 hours after; 8 per 24 hours for high risk patients (alcohol use, low potassium, malnutrition, liver disease)

steps.q: Sodium rose 12 mmol/L in 12 hours. What now?

options.t: Stop hypertonic fluid; give hypotonic fluid with or without desmopressin per protocol

cases.pearl: **Seizure: 3% bolus for a 4 to 6 rise. Then no more than 8 to 10 per 24 h.**

sources.t: Society for Endocrinology: Emergency management of severe hyponatraemia (2022)
MacMillan TE, et al. Osmotic demyelination syndrome in patients hospitalized with hyponatremia. NEJM Evid 2023
St. Mary's ICU drip concentrations, electrolyte and insulin protocols (verify locally)

workup.calc: 3% saline 100 to 150 mL over 10 to 20 min, up to about 3 times. Na 112: aim for about 116 to 118 in the first hours; no more than about 122 at 24 hours (10 per 24 h), 120 if high risk (8 per 24 h).

cases.title: ICU glucose target
cases.stem: Glucose 240 and 260 on two checks in a ventilated patient. The team wants a target of 80 to 110.

steps.q: What target do ADA and AACE recommend?

options.t: Start insulin above 180; target 140 to 180 mg/dL

options.why: NICE-SUGAR: tight control raised 90 day death (27.5% vs 24.9%) and severe lows (6.8% vs 0.5%).

sources.t: NICE-SUGAR Study Investigators. Intensive vs conventional glucose control in critically ill patients. N Engl J Med 2009;360:1283-1297

cases.title: DKA: potassium before insulin
cases.stem: Glucose 520, pH 7.08, bicarbonate 8, beta hydroxybutyrate 6.1. K 3.2 mmol/L. Weight 70 kg.

steps.q: Can the insulin infusion start now?

options.t: No: hold insulin and replace potassium until K is 3.5 or higher (2024 consensus)
options.why: Insulin drives potassium into cells and can cause a fatal arrhythmia.
It is the first safety check.

steps.q: Once K is 3.5, what insulin regimen?

options.t: Fixed rate IV regular insulin 0.1 units/kg/h (7 units/h), no routine bolus
options.why: 2024 consensus; a bolus only if IV access is delayed.

steps.q: Glucose falls to 230. What changes?

options.t: Add D5 or D10 to fluids and lower insulin to 0.05 units/kg/h; keep insulin running until ketones clear

steps.q: When can the drip stop?

options.t: DKA resolved (beta hydroxybutyrate below 0.6 and pH 7.3 or more or bicarbonate 18 or more) and SC basal insulin given 1 to 2 hours before stopping
options.why: Overlap prevents a gap with no insulin.

cases.pearl: **DKA: K 3.5 first, 0.1 units/kg/h no bolus, dextrose at 250, overlap basal 1 to 2 h.**

sources.t: Umpierrez GE, et al. Hyperglycemic crises in adults with diabetes: consensus report. Diabetes Care 2024;47:1257-1275
St. Mary's ICU drip concentrations, electrolyte and insulin protocols (verify locally)

workup.calc: K 3.2: hold insulin, replace potassium. Then 0.1 units/kg/h x 70 kg = **7 units/h**; at glucose below 250: 0.05 units/kg/h = **3.5 units/h** plus dextrose.

cases.title: IV potassium rates
cases.stem: K 2.9, Mg 1.3. Peripheral IV only. Order: KCl 40 mEq IV over 1 hour.

steps.q: What is wrong?

options.t: 40 mEq/h is far above the usual peripheral limit of 10 mEq/h
options.why: Faster rates need a central line and continuous ECG per policy; the label reserves up to 40 mEq/h for urgent K below 2.0 with ECG changes or paralysis.

steps.q: What else must be fixed?

options.t: Replace magnesium too; low magnesium makes potassium hard to correct
options.why: Low Mg keeps the kidney losing potassium.

steps.q: Can KCl ever be pushed IV?

options.why: IV push potassium can cause cardiac arrest.

cases.pearl: **Peripheral K: 10 mEq/h max. Fix magnesium. Never push.**

sources.t: FDA label, Potassium Chloride Injection (highly concentrated, 2019)
St. Mary's ICU drip concentrations, electrolyte and insulin protocols (verify locally)

workup.calc: 40 mEq at the 10 mEq/h peripheral limit = **4 hours**, not 1. Replace Mg 1.3 as well.

cases.title: Stress ulcer prophylaxis
cases.stem: Three ICU patients are on pantoprazole: (A) on a ventilator only, eating tube feeds, no other risk; (B) septic shock on norepinephrine; (C) INR 2.8 from liver disease.

steps.q: Who has an indication under SCCM/ASHP 2024?

options.t: C: coagulopathy and chronic liver disease
A: ventilator alone with tube feeds
options.why: Mechanical ventilation alone is not an established indication.

steps.q: When should it stop?

options.t: When the risk resolves or at ICU transfer
options.why: A common source of unneeded discharge PPIs.

cases.pearl: **SUP for shock, coagulopathy, liver disease. Stop when risk ends.**

sources.t: SCCM/ASHP 2024 guideline: stress ulcer prophylaxis in critically ill adults

cases.title: Shift simulation: ICU night
cases.stem: Four calls: (1) K 7.0 with wide QRS; (2) a pressor bag will run out in 20 minutes; (3) a question about switching a PPI to IV; (4) a TPN label question for tomorrow.

steps.q: First?

options.t: K 7.0 with wide QRS: calcium now

options.why: Twenty minutes allows calcium first, then the bag.

steps.q: Second?

options.t: Get the replacement pressor bag ready before the current one runs out

cases.pearl: **Arrest risk, then drips that cannot stop, then routine.**

sources.t: Clase CM, et al. Potassium homeostasis and management of dyskalemia (KDIGO). Kidney Int 2020;97:42-61
FDA label, Norepinephrine Bitartrate in Sodium Chloride (2022)
